title: CRASH-078: array diff intersect globals symtable alias bucket uaf (use-after-free)
live_proof: measured, not asserted: our native ASan build of the pinned 5.0.0 tarball (p12, gcc 15.2.0, libasan from gcc 15, 2026-10-27) reports ASAN:heap-use-after-free at ext/standard/array.c:171 in array_key_compare when trigger.php runs; the corpus records the fix as php-src 96d755978cc8, which postdates the release, and names the defect at ext/standard/array.c:3273 (defect: *return_value = **args[0]; zval_copy_ctor no-ops for &EG(symbol_table)); crash frame ext/standard/array.c:171
fidelity: the corpus's own trigger script, run through the real interpreter (PHP's cli SAPI, ext/standard only, the port's 145 translation units) rather than reduced to a C model. What it does NOT establish is which arm ought to catch it. The pristine build completes it natively, so an arm that completes it saw nothing.
fault_sites_why: ASan's access stack in our native run (results-ours-asan-default.json, sha256 045e3366bfc5) has array_key_compare at ext/standard/array.c:171 as its first frame inside PHP's tree (frame #0); the stack's remaining frames are the interpreter's dispatch and are not sites

cheribsd-revocation.oracle: the same trigger on stock CheriBSD purecap -- no nested layer at all, the real interpreter cross-built by ports/php/cheribsd/build.sh -- in the boot at the platform default (security.cheri.runtime_revocation_default=1, every_free=0): a SIGPROT at the ASan site with the bounds-malloc control faulting in the same boot, the same binary run with revocation off as the pair that attributes the fault, or the trigger ends and this arm did not see it (tools/arms.json cheribsd-default)
cheribsd-revocation.verdict_note: reached (route B: the trigger printed its own output, so it ran: array(0) {) and completed with no fault; NOT-REISSUED: no capability fault at the platform default, but the eager configuration (runtime_revocation_every_free_default=1) faults on this case, so the stale pointer IS followed. The eager fault lands inside the script body, which is what tells a revoked object apart from the allocator's cache being drained back to libc at shutdown. Context, not a verdict: every-free also faults on accesses nothing is meant to catch
